chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and life on the road
title: Favourite rooms and the Johns Manville jazz parties in Denver
summary: She liked the Hyatt hotels in New Orleans and Indianapolis. Johns Manville's president Mr. Goodwin held annual jazz parties in Denver where she got a huge suite, a limousine and catered parties.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: Well, there is one thing that makes a difference and that's the type of room you're working.
Yeah.

You know, some rooms are sympathetic rooms, whether it's the size of them or whether it's the sort of people that come to them. But you've got favorite rooms. Well, you like that Hyatt-Regency, don't you?
Oh yeah, I did. I liked that. And I did the Hyatt in Indianapolis.

Did you?
Yes.
What was that like?
It was lovely.
What sort of accomodations did you have there? Nice?
Yeah.

Well, I don't want to side track you, but one time you told me, two or three years ago, you said, and it might have even been a private party that you did but you told me you were out somewhere and I had the impression it was the mid-west, and you said it was the most gorgeous place. You said you had a big suite.
Oh, that was the Johns Mansville in Denver. Oh that was, I've never had nothing like that before.
What wasthat like?
It was just like living like a millionaire because I had a great big two bedroom, two bathroom suite by myself with a living room, dining room, kitchen and bar. That was just for me.

How long were you there?
Just there for two, three days.
They probably thought you were going to bring alot of friends in.
Yeah, well you could have. One time I did bring some friends. But then the boys had one too.
Who were the boys? Was it Jerry?
Yeah, Jerry and Major Holly.
They had a suite too?

Yeah. And one time I took Ellis Larkins with me, and him and Major, I think it was, they shared a suite. But there were two bedrooms, two baths, a kitchen, and a dining room and living room, you know. And then they would have people come in and cater a party for us.
For heaven's sake.
And the bars would be loaded. So you see . .
So all the hospitality wasn't always your's.
No, it wasn't. But that's something else there.

Johns Hopkins, is that the hospital group?
No, Johns Mansville. The richest man in the world.
Oh, was he having a private party?
Well, the resident and Mr. Goodwin, they used to have these jazz parties, you know, every year. And I was always one of the guests.
Oh for heaven's sake. You did it several times?
Yeah. And then he gave you a limousine at your service.
It certainly makes a difference doesn't it?
Yeah, don't it though? Yes indeed. Anything you wanted you got.
Isn't that terrific. That's wonderful.
I sure was sorry when Mr. Goodwin wasn't president anymore because this many they got there now, well he's not a jazz fan and I don't know what's happening now. I'm so sorry about that.
